source.title: Two types of dopamine neuron distinctly convey positive and negative motivational signals

confidence_rationale: Direct primate electrophysiology showing that midbrain dopamine neurons split into two functionally and anatomically distinct populations during a Pavlovian task with both appetitive (reward) and aversive (airpuff) outcomes: a minority 'value-coding' group excited by reward-predicting cues and inhibited by airpuff-predicting cues (a signed channel), and a majority 'salience-coding' group excited by both (an unsigned/motivational-salience channel). The two groups are anatomically segregated (dorsolateral vs ventromedial SNc/VTA). This is the most direct primate evidence this corpus holds that a signed valence channel and a non-signed salience channel are computed by separable dopaminergic populations rather than one blended signal -- the specific structural claim MECH-054 makes about signed harm/benefit precision channels remaining distinct. Confidence is not higher because (a) the paper's 'signed' population is the minority, not the majority, of recorded neurons, complicating a direct 'this IS the MECH-054 channel' identification, and (b) the task uses simple Pavlovian cue-outcome pairs (liquid reward vs airpuff), not the graded, harm-vs-benefit residue-field valence structure REE models.
failure_signatures: The anatomically-segregated 'value-coding' dopamine population is a minority of recorded neurons; most dopamine neurons in this dataset are salience-coding (excited by both reward- and aversive-predicting cues), so a strict 'dopamine = signed valence' reading is not what the paper shows -- it shows a mixture, with signed coding as one identifiable component

Anatomical segregation (dorsolateral vs ventromedial SNc/VTA) is correlational with response type in this dataset; the paper does not causally manipulate one population to show it alone carries signed information

The aversive stimulus (airpuff) is a low-level noxious/startle stimulus, not the graded, contextual harm signal REE's harm stream represents -- transfer from 'airpuff' to 'harm residue field' is an inferential step

mapping.source_claim_statement: In monkeys performing a Pavlovian task with reward (liquid) and aversive (airpuff) outcomes, a subset of dopamine neurons was excited by reward-predicting cues and inhibited by airpuff-predicting cues (signed, value-coding), while a larger subset was excited by both reward- and airpuff-predicting cues (unsigned, salience-coding). The two response types were found in anatomically distinct locations -- value-coding neurons more ventromedial (including VTA), salience-coding neurons more dorsolateral (SNc).
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-054 claims that signed harm and benefit prediction-error precision channels remain computationally distinct rather than collapsing into one blended valence signal. Matsumoto & Hikosaka's anatomical and functional dissociation of a signed (value-coding) dopamine population from an unsigned (salience-coding) one is direct primate evidence that the brain implements at least two separable channels at the dopaminergic output stage, one of which specifically preserves sign. This supports MECH-054's structural claim that signed and unsigned (or oppositely-signed) precision-weighted error channels are not merged by the time they reach downstream valuation circuits.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's 'signed' population is a minority of recorded dopamine neurons, so the mapping is 'a signed channel exists and is anatomically separable' rather than 'dopamine output is predominantly signed' -- MECH-054 does not require the latter, but a reader should not over-read this as showing dopamine is generally a clean signed-PE signal. The stimuli (liquid reward, airpuff) are simple unconditioned outcomes, not the graded contextual harm/benefit residue fields REE models, so the 'precision' component of MECH-054 (channel reliability/weighting, not just sign) is not directly tested here -- this paper evidences the sign-separation half of the claim, not the precision-weighting half.
mapping.source_context: Primate (rhesus macaque), Pavlovian conditioning with liquid reward and airpuff-to-face aversive outcomes, in-vivo single-unit recording from substantia nigra pars compacta and ventral tegmental area dopamine neurons, anatomical localisation of recording sites.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: Nature, primate single-unit recording, anatomically localised, from the same group (Matsumoto & Hikosaka) whose lateral habenula work already anchors this corpus's MECH-053/054 coverage. Mapping fidelity moderate: strong for the 'sign-separable channels exist' half of MECH-054, weaker for the 'precision' (reliability-weighting) half, which this paper does not address. Transfer risk moderate: simple Pavlovian outcomes vs REE's graded residue-field valence.
